# A workflow file holds the structure of its jobs, and nothing else

A file of `.github/workflows/` names its jobs, their triggers, their conditions, their runners and what they call.
The path-filter data is in `.github/ci-areas.yaml`, one package area a job, which `dorny/paths-filter` reads by path, in one step of `ci.yaml`'s `changes` job, and which holds less than 10,000 bytes.
The steps of a job of `ci.yaml` are a composite action under `.github/actions/<job>/`, one subfolder a leg where a leg has steps of its own, and `ci.yaml` names the job, its legs, its gate and the action it runs.
A `run:` body of more than 10 lines is a script under `.github/scripts/`, run by its path, with each budget comment on the line it sizes, but for two kinds of job.
A body stays inline where its job makes no checkout, and where its job holds a credential of a release workflow, as `release.yaml`'s publish job does, because `.github/scripts/check-release-credentials.sh` refuses a credentialed job that runs any script under a `scripts/` directory but `.github/scripts/release-push.sh` and `.github/scripts/check-private-names.sh`, each run by its path behind `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/`.
The longer bodies of `ci.yaml`, `dispatch-browser.yaml`, `release.yaml` and the tool-fallback job are moved, but for those two kinds of job; a timed body moved into an action keeps a `timeout` command around it, and a timed `uses:` step stays a step of `ci.yaml` with its own `timeout-minutes`.
The bodies of the other workflow files are not moved yet, and a file that reaches the size limit moves its bodies then, as the size check's refusal says.
A derivation or a history goes in `.github/ci-notes/<the workflow file's name without its suffix>.md` (the tool-fallback job's in `tool-fallback.md`), and the step it belongs to keeps one comment line, `# why: .github/ci-notes/<file>.md#<the section's anchor>`, that names it; a value's own arithmetic stays on its line in the workflow file.
`.github/scripts/check-ci-layout.sh` refuses a section no such line names and a line naming no section.
`.github/scripts/check-workflow-files.sh` holds every file of that directory to 64,000 bytes and `ci.yaml` to 63,000, refuses one GitHub's own parser would not read (invalid YAML, or two keys of one mapping that are equal when upper-cased) and one that calls more than 10 unique reusable workflows, nested calls included, holds the filter text a paths-filter step reads to less than 10,000 bytes, and holds `ci.yaml` to 32 jobs besides the carriers of a split job's old name.
It also refuses a job or step that sets `JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` or `STEP_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` to anything but the `timeout-minutes` it stands for, or sets either where it stands for no one limit, and a step that has a `timeout-minutes` of its own, reaches `.github/scripts/gh-read.sh` and sets no `STEP_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` (that script waits for GitHub's rate limits within those numbers).
The number is 64,000 because GitHub starts no run at all for a workflow file above its cap of 500 KB and signals that only as a run with no jobs in it, so the limit a reader is held to is a readable file rather than a parser's limit.
`ci.yaml`'s lint job runs the check, `.github/workflows/workflow-files.yaml` runs it a second time in a file small enough to start when `ci.yaml` is too large to, and `ci.yaml`'s scripts-held job (`test / test`) runs `.github/scripts/check-workflow-files.test.sh`.
actionlint 1.7.12 checks every workflow file in those same two places, with `.github/actionlint.yaml`, and the shellcheck 0.11.0 it hands each inline `run:` body reads at warning severity, so a finding of either fails the pull request; `.github/scripts/check-action-shell.sh` runs that shellcheck over the `run:` bodies of the composite actions and the scripts of `.github/scripts/`, which actionlint does not read.
Run what CI runs before you push a workflow change, from the root of a git checkout, since actionlint finds no project outside one: `SHELLCHECK_OPTS=--severity=warning go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.12 -shellcheck='uvx --from shellcheck-py@0.11.0.1 shellcheck' -verbose`
